clue.text: A root to watch

definitions.meaning: a root vegetable, the swede's white cousin
old slang for a large, thick pocket watch

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on a root vegetable growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a root vegetable and, in old slang, a bulky pocket timepiece.

clue.text: Employers are entertaining, after taking the morning off

indicators.note: taking signals that something is to be removed from the word for entertainers
off completes the removal, saying the morning is stripped from the front

parts.note: those who are entertaining are amusers
AM is the abbreviation for morning

explanation.surface: Bosses lay on fun after giving staff the morning off.
explanation.walkthrough: AMUSERS (those who are entertaining) loses AM (morning), leaving those who employ things.
explanation.definitionFit: Users are people who employ something, in the sense of making use of it.

clue.text: Point to a tailless bird I brought in to the city

indicators.note: brought in means the letter I is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass

indicators.note: tailless means the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: the robin is a common garden bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail is pointed out and brought into town.
explanation.walkthrough: N (a compass point), A and ROBI (ROBIN without its tail), with I put between A and ROBI. Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Fish can disseminate energy, maybe?

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: to disseminate is to scatter, so the letters of can are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Perhaps fish can spread energy about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disseminate' scatters CAN into ANC; PERCH goes before it and E (energy) after.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: Opening serves can unfortunately lose direction

indicators.note: unfortunately says the letters of serves can have come out badly and in a new order
lose tells us to drop a letter from the rearranged words

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A tennis player's serves, aimed badly, miss their target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges SERVES CAN, which 'lose direction' says hold the answer plus N (north): drop the N and the other eight letters make the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack or fissure in a glacier, an opening in the ice.

clue.text: Animal juggling act

indicators.note: juggling tosses things about, so the letters of act are rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus performance in which a creature juggles.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is a domestic animal, a feline pet.

clue.text: Quiet apprentice supporting the board

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the learner's letter beneath the word for quiet

parts.note: ease is peace and quiet, rest
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee quietly props up a board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an easel is the stand on which an artist's board rests, so the clue names the thing by what it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the frame an artist's board or canvas sits on, so it stands in for the board's mount.

clue.text: Passage through which one should move briskly

definitions.text: Passage through which one should move briskly

parts.words: Passage through which one should move briskly
parts.note: a passage sounds like a corridor to hurry along, but it is a section of music marked to be played at a lively pace

explanation.surface: A corridor where one is expected to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo marking for fast and lively labels a passage played briskly.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing — hadn't got a shirt to call his own

definitions.text: hadn't got a shirt to call his own
definitions.meaning: read literally, without a shift, an old word for a shirt or chemise

explanation.surface: A layabout too poor to own a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiftless person is idle and feckless; and a shift is an old name for a shirt, so without one means shirtless.

clue.text: Runs down as tiger is driven out from lair

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's lair

indicators.note: something driven out is forced from its place, signalling the letters of as tiger are dislodged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiger is chased out of its lair, as hunters run it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs down' means disparages, not chases. 'is driven out' rearranges AS TIGER to IGRATES, which goes after DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down someone is to belittle or disparage them.

clue.text: Late-starter, second-rate, cheer leader — being worldly

annotationWithheld.why: Late-starter, second-rate, cheer leader — being worldly (4): L + ? + C; nothing in the clue as held gives AI (A1 is first-rate, not second-rate), so a word looks misprinted or garbled and no source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Late-starter, second-rate, cheer leader — being worldly

clue.text: City's very large — look!

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
lo is an old word meaning look! or behold!

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how huge a city is.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: They may be seen playing on the lanes at night

definitions.text: They may be seen playing on the lanes at night

parts.words: They may be seen playing on the lanes at night
parts.note: playing suggests musicians or children on country lanes, but here it means beams of light shining on the road from a car after dark

explanation.surface: Performers or children seen playing in country lanes after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Car lamps at the front of a vehicle throw beams that play over the road at night.

clue.text: Rat trapped in a sunken valley — the perfect place

indicators.note: trapped in means the word for rat is held inside the other letters

parts.note: a ria is a drowned river valley on a coast
a cad is a rat, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rat is caught in a flooded valley, hardly paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: A ria is a coastal valley drowned by the sea; CAD sits inside A RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised pastoral paradise of Greek legend, a byword for an ideal spot.

clue.text: Behaviour getting airman into trouble

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up or disturb, so the letters of into are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's conduct lands a young airman in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' reads as part of 'get into trouble' but is the anagram fodder: 'trouble' turns INTO into TION, after AC (aircraftman).
explanation.definitionFit: Action is conduct or deeds, what someone does, as is behaviour.

clue.text: She could be so rich, see?

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of so rich see might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be so wealthy, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: A woman sharing an inheritance could well be rich, so the whole clue hints at the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheiress is a woman who inherits jointly with another, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Doctor cures Tom — he's always right

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters of cures Tom are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor heals a patient called Tom, who insists he knows best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician who cures Tom but is the anagram signal. The definition plays on the shop saying 'the customer is always right'.
explanation.definitionFit: The retail maxim says the buyer is always right, so the phrase describes a shopper.

clue.text: Temporary bed that pulls out?

definitions.meaning: a litter for carrying the sick or wounded
something that extends or pulls taut, a device that lengthens

explanation.surface: A folding bed that extends.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a litter for carrying a patient, and literally a thing that pulls something longer.

clue.text: Despatch cover for instrument — make a point of it!

indicators.note: cover means the word for despatch wraps round the instrument

parts.note: to despatch something is to send it
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone sends a protective case for a musical instrument and insists on doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a point of it' sounds like insisting, but it describes the pointed end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp end of a blade or tool is its point, the part that is made pointed.

clue.text: British economist set free, without a car and with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the zero after the rest
without in its old sense of outside means the word for set free goes round the car

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A British economist is freed, car-less and naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: RID goes round CAR, and O (nothing) comes on after. David Ricardo was the classical economist.
explanation.definitionFit: David Ricardo was a leading classical economist of early nineteenth-century Britain.

clue.text: Time off from regiment — most unusual

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British Army regiment
rest is time off work

explanation.surface: A soldier gets leave from the regiment, a rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just sets REST next to RA; the charade reads RA then REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, so it means least common.

clue.text: Race past and keep running to get a place

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to race
go on means to keep running or continue

explanation.surface: A runner sprints by and keeps going to finish placed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangoon, now Yangon, is the former capital of Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is a city in Myanmar, the old Burmese capital.

clue.text: Magic broomstick

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a broomstick is the vehicle that a witch flies on, her craft

explanation.surface: A conjuror's enchanted broom.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches' sorcery is magic; and a broomstick is, punningly, the flying vessel a sorceress rides.

clue.text: Blows on the wrists?

definitions.meaning: slaps or smacks with the hand
the turned-back ends of sleeves at the wrists

explanation.surface: Slaps across the wrists.
explanation.definitionFit: Light blows with the open hand share a name with the bands of a sleeve at the wrist.

clue.text: Fellow turning key and then knob

indicators.note: turning means the word for a fellow is read backwards

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone turns a key and then a doorknob.
explanation.walkthrough: A don, a college fellow, read backwards gives NOD; E is a key in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or lump, such as a swelling on a stem or joint.

clue.text: Crowded together, being stupid

explanation.surface: Packed in and thick-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense describes things packed tightly and, of a person, someone slow to understand.

clue.text: Poet said to smirk

indicators.note: said means we want a word that sounds like the word for smirk

parts.note: to leer is to smirk or look slyly

explanation.surface: A poet is reported to wear a smug grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the English writer of nonsense verse and limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Welsh migrant discovered to have injury

indicators.note: to have means the word for discovered holds the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: found means discovered

indicators.note: a migrant moves from place to place, so the letters of Welsh wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A Welshman working abroad turns out to have been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'migrant' rearranges WELSH to LESHW, which goes inside FOUND (discovered) after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A flesh wound is a superficial injury that cuts the skin but spares bone and organs.

clue.text: The aim is a conclusive one

explanation.surface: The goal is a decisive one.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a goal, as in means to an end, and also the finish or close of something.

clue.text: Advocated getting married in the old-fashioned way

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense of wed or betrothed

explanation.surface: Someone backed a traditional church wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support it; in archaic use to espouse someone is to take them in marriage.

clue.text: Carpet an athlete

definitions.meaning: a long narrow rug for a hall or stairs

explanation.surface: A rug is likened to a sportsperson.
explanation.definitionFit: A long strip of carpet along a corridor shares its name with one who races on the track.
